subject: Inference session resync: customer-facing summary & action playbook
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@skycap.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@skycap.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inference session resync: customer-facing summary & action playbook

Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for patience while we finished our internal investigation. Attached is a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we fixed, and the concrete actions you can expect from us over the next 30 days. I wanted to call out the highlights up front and make it easy to pick the items most relevant to SkyCap.

Executive summary
- Incident window: 2028-05-19T22:38:00Z to 2028-05-19T23:15:00Z (recovery and validation continued through 2028-05-20T02:00:00Z).
- Impact: Intermittent 502/timeout errors and duplicated token output for a small subset (~0.6%) of inference sessions pinned to dedicated pool #dc-west-3. Latency spikes for affected sessions (tail 99.9th) and a handful of failed requests that retried.
- Root cause (short): A race in the session manager's resync path caused stale KV cache shards to be reattached to active sessions under specific reconnect timing, producing mismatched KV offsets and duplicated token emission when KV replay occurred.

What we fixed (already deployed)
1) Patch: We released v2.14.3 to the serving runtime that short-circuits session resync if the KV epoch does not match the expected generation. This prevents stale shards from reattaching. (Deployed 2028-05-20T01:12:00Z)
2) Short-term mitigation: We added a conservative fallback that rejects immediate reconnects from sessions reporting epoch mismatch and forces a cold-start with KV rebuild. This reduced the error rate to baseline for affected pools.
3) Observability: New metric (session_kv_epoch_mismatch) and an alert that triggers at 0.1% of active sessions; logs for full replay for forensic evidence collection have been enabled for 72 hours and archived. Evidence bundle attached.

Customer impact and timeline (high level)
- 22:35Z — first elevated 502 alerts from pooling layer.
- 22:38Z — increased error rate; on-call engaged and mitigations initiated.
- 22:55Z — root-cause hypothesis (session resync) validated using request traces and KV timeline scan.
- 23:05Z — patch candidate validated in staging; rolled to canary.
- 23:15Z — canary shows no recurrence; full rollout initiated.
- 01:12Z — v2.14.3 fully rolled; post-deploy validation completed.

Action playbook for SkyCap (owners and ETA)
- Customer verification call: schedule within 72 hours to review evidence and confirm no downstream data issues. Owner: David Kim (owner: david_kim@redwood.ai).
- Action ledger (attached): step-by-step deliverables, owners, and deadlines. Owner: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai).
- Long-term code change: introduce an epoch-consistent resync protocol (design doc in progress). ETA: 2028-06-15. Owner: Hannah Schmitt (hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai).
- Billing review / goodwill: team will propose a usage credit for affected requests after verification. Owner: Sean Gallagher (sean.gallagher@redwood.ai).

Requested next steps from you
- Please confirm a 60-minute window in the next 72 hours for a verification + Q&A call (we recommend 2028-05-21 10:00-11:00 PT or 2028-05-22 14:00-15:00 PT).
- If you want raw traces or a more detailed forensic export beyond the attached bundle, say which time ranges and we'll prioritize.

Attachments: postmortem_summary.pdf (this file), evidence-logs.zip (samples and folded traces), action_ledger.xlsx (owner tracker).

Thanks — and apologies for the disruption. We'll treat this as high priority and keep you closely updated until all ledger items are complete.

--
David Kim
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

David —

Thanks for the quick and thorough write-up. A couple of clarifying questions from our engineering and billing teams:
1) Can you quantify how many unique SkyCap sessions were affected during the window (approximate count or percentage of our requests)?
2) For the evidence export, can you include the full trace for request id 0a1b2c3d (we saw duplicated tokens there) and the upstream load-balancer logs for the same time range?
3) Regarding credits: we appreciate the offer — can you outline the proposed credit approach and timing? Our procurement team will need this for approvals.

We can do the 2028-05-22 14:00-15:00 PT slot for the verification call. Please send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the transparency — we rely on Redwood for production inference and want to ensure we capture any leftover concerns for our compliance audit.

--
Laura Jenkins
VP Engineering, SkyCap Payments
laura.jenkins@skycap.com

1) Affected session count: preliminary estimate is ~2.1k unique sessions tied to your dedicated pool slice (~0.6% of SkyCap's total requests in the window). We'll provide exact counts from the trace export by EOD 2028-05-21 once the log fold is complete. (Owner: Marissa)

2) Evidence export: full traces for request id 0a1b2c3d plus LB logs will be included in evidence-logs.zip and uploaded to the Drive link (shared). (Owner: David)

3) Credits approach: Sean to propose a credit framework by 2028-05-22 morning; we will tie credits to verified failed/duplicated requests in the ledger and finalize on the verification call. (Owner: Sean Gallagher)

4) Post-call deliverables: we will produce a short technical appendix to the summary that shows the KV epoch mismatch trace, a defensive checklist for customer-side retry behavior, and the design doc for the long-term protocol change. ETA for appendix and design doc links: 2028-06-01. (Owner: Hannah)

5) Runbook update: immediate playbook change scheduled to prevent reconnects within 3s of an epoch mismatch; new test added to CI. (Owner: Marissa)

Marissa — please start the exact-count export and note the retention requirements for the evidence bundle. David — I'll prep the design doc skeleton and invite the service owners. Sean — flag any billing constraints we should be aware of before proposing credits.

Thanks —

Appended deliverables ahead of our 2028-05-22 call (and follow-up notes after the call):
- Evidence bundle uploaded (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-post-incident-evidence — includes full traces for 0a1b2c3d and LB logs.
- Action ledger (attached) populated with exact counts and timestamps. Key ledger items:
  • Confirmed affected sessions: 2,134 unique SkyCap sessions (0.57% of requests in the window).
  • Duplicate-token verified events: 48 requests tied to retried sessions; detailed list in action_ledger.xlsx.
  • Credit proposal: 100% credit for verified failed requests (48), pro-rated for retries (see ledger). Sean will post the formal credit note to procurement by EOD 2028-05-23.
- Runbook & CI: immediate test added and merged to staging; production rollback guard created to prevent re-deploys without epoch-mismatch alerts suppressed.

Next milestones (short):
- 2028-05-24: post-verification audit (internal + SkyCap) to confirm ledger items and close evidence export.
- 2028-06-15: delivery of epoch-consistent resync protocol RFC and prototype.

I've attached action_ledger.xlsx to this message and included the signed commitment rows. If you need a DocuSign or formal SOW addendum for credits, we can route that through procurement and I can coordinate with Sean.

Thanks again for your collaboration — we'll stay on top of every ledger item until you're satisfied.
